# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about this carefully. I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind cannot see anything I do. Blind can only receive information through speech from someone who can speak - but I cannot speak, and Deaf cannot speak either! Let me check the roles again.

Wait - only Blind cannot speak either. Let me recheck: Mute cannot speak, Blind cannot touch... wait, Blind CAN speak (nothing says otherwise). Looking at the table: Deaf cannot hear or touch. Mute cannot speak or touch. Blind cannot see.

So Blind can speak and hear. Deaf can see but not hear/speak (not touch). Mute can see and hear but not speak, not touch.

So: I (Mute) can gesture to Deaf. Deaf can see my gestures but cannot speak - so Deaf cannot relay to Blind via speech. Deaf also cannot touch. Blind can speak and hear, so Blind can hear Deaf? No - Deaf cannot speak, only gesture. Blind cannot see gestures.

So the only link from me to Blind is: Mute gestures to Deaf (Deaf sees) → but Deaf cannot speak to pass it to Blind, and Blind can't see gestures. Dead end unless Deaf gestures too - but Blind can't see that either.

Actually Blind can speak - so Blind's words reach Mute and Deaf (both can hear). I need to encode "purple" via gestures to Deaf, but Deaf then needs to tell Blind - Deaf cannot speak. So the chain must go: I gesture a code to Deaf, Deaf matches gesture code to a color they see on the bomb, then Deaf... cannot speak to Blind either.

Turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. So Deaf speaks last - wait Deaf cannot speak at all. So Blind must be the one relaying, since Blind can speak. Blind can hear me? No, I cannot speak. Blind cannot see my gestures.

The only path: I gesture to Deaf. Deaf sees the bomb's colors and my gesture-code. Deaf cannot speak, but Deaf could gesture back confirmation - useless for Blind. Blind needs verbal instruction, which must come from Blind itself (self-talk) or from Deaf - but Deaf can't speak.

So actually the critical link is: Deaf must gesture to convey info toward... only Mute can see Deaf's gestures too (I can see). But I already know the manual. So I need to receive from Deaf which wire is purple isn't needed - I need to send "cut purple" to Blind, but Blind can't see gestures and I can't speak.

Therefore: I gesture a code to Deaf that Deaf can translate into speech for Blind, since Deaf... cannot speak. Wait, rereading: Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" - speaking isn't prohibited for Deaf! Let me recheck table: only listed cannots. Deaf cannot: hear, touch. Deaf CAN speak.

That changes everything - Deaf can speak to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a strip with three engraved marks, pattern is symbol-symbol-symbol where first and third look the same shape and the middle is different. Keypad has four keys engraved 1 through 4 with numbers 6, 8, 7, 0 respectively, and a display area expecting 1 digit, currently nothing entered. There are 6 wires I can cut but I cannot tell their colors. What does the manual say to do first?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Good, Blind confirmed they can speak and hear. Deaf can see the bomb's colors but cannot speak - wait, I concluded last turn Deaf CAN speak. But Deaf only gestured, didn't speak. Let me not assume - maybe Deaf truly cannot speak (re-reading original rules: "Deaf: Can See the bomb... Cannot Hear anything, or touch the bomb" - speaking isn't restricted for Deaf per that table, but maybe the intent is Deaf simply has no reason to speak since nobody said they can't... Actually wait, the turn order and channel description only says "When you gesture, Deaf receives it. You cannot speak." for me. For Deaf, its channels probably let it speak too, but it only gestured this turn - maybe it doesn't know it can speak, or maybe it truly cannot).

Given ambiguity, I must work with what's given: Deaf gestures to me, I see gestures. Blind speaks and hears - so Blind can hear Deaf if Deaf speaks. Since Deaf only used gesture, perhaps Deaf actually cannot speak (only I was told explicitly "you cannot speak" as Mute - meaning maybe only Mute has that restriction named explicitly, but table shows Deaf's cannots don't include speaking, so Deaf should be able to). I'll test by asking Deaf via gesture to speak the color to Blind directly.

I need a gesture code for "purple". I'll assign: ☝ = attention/first instruction. Let me establish a color-gesture alphabet with Deaf and instruct them to relay to Blind by speaking the color name.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫶", "👉", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display shows 7, light is yellow, strip painted blue red red, wires in order are blue yellow orange red purple white. Keypad numbers I feel are 6 8 7 0 for slots 1 2 3 4. Display value 7 matches slot 3 which is engraved 7. Does the manual say anything about matching display number to keypad, or about wire colors, or about light color, or about a strip with two same colors and one different?
Deaf says to Mute: display now shows 6, light is red, changed from before. strip still blue red red. keypad still 1:6 2:8 3:7 4:0 wants 1 digit. wires unchanged 1 blue 2 yellow 3 orange 4 red 5 purple 6 white. does the manual need the display number, light color, strip colors, keypad digit, or a wire color? gesture back which one matters most using pointing or numbers if you can.

Excellent - Deaf CAN speak, and just spoke directly to Blind and to me. This confirms Deaf can speak. Now I can just gesture simple confirmation to Deaf, and Deaf can relay in words to Blind. The manual says: cut the purple wire. Wire 5 is purple per Deaf's report. I need to tell them wire color matters, specifically purple, position 5.

I'll gesture a code Deaf can map to "wire color, the purple one, position 5". Since gestures only carry symbols with no inherent meaning, I need to define a simple scheme. Let me use numbers via finger-count-like symbols to indicate "wire" category and position 5, and point to purple concept indirectly - but Deaf already knows which wire is purple (they can see colors). I just need to say "cut the purple wire" - I need Deaf to know "purple" is the answer among the wire colors they see.

I'll establish: ☝ = "wire color matters". Then a number gesture for position. Deaf listed wires with positions 1-6, purple is position 5. I'll gesture ☝ then 🖐 (5 fingers) to indicate wire, position 5.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent: display just changed from 7 to 6, light changed from yellow to red. This may be a timer - I may need to act soon. Please tell me immediately what the manual says about display-to-keypad matching, light colors, or wire order, even if partial.
Deaf says to Mute: i cannot tell what your gestures mean yet. let's use fingers as numbers: hold up 1 finger for display, 2 for light, 3 for strip, 4 for keypad, 5 for wires, to tell me which one the manual cares about first. i will then ask yes or no questions and you gesture thumbs up for yes thumbs down for no.

Deaf proposed a clear protocol - I should follow it. I already gestured 5 (wires) last turn, but they said they couldn't interpret it yet. Let me redo per their scheme: hold up 5 for wires.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: i think you gestured 5, meaning wires matter. gesture thumbs up if wires is correct, thumbs down if not. if wires is correct, i will ask about which wire to cut using finger counts 1 through 6.

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: good, wires confirmed. gesture the wire number to cut using finger count 1 through 6, one hand, one gesture. if the manual says cut by color not number, gesture an open hand with all five fingers spread twice instead.

Purple is wire 5 based on Deaf's earlier report (1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white). The manual says cut the purple wire, which corresponds to position 5 in Deaf's list. I'll gesture 5.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Pattern noticed: light color seems to match a wire color each time - blue light when wire1 is blue, yellow light when wire2 is yellow, red light when wire4 is red. Maybe light color tells us which wire to cut. Please confirm with manual if light color determines the wire.
Deaf says to Mute: i see one open hand, five fingers. i am reading that as wire 5, purple. gesture thumbs up if wire 5 purple is correct, thumbs down if not.

Deaf correctly identified wire 5 as purple, matching the manual instruction. I need to confirm this is correct - the manual simply says cut the purple wire, and wire 5 is purple, regardless of light color patterns (that's Blind's speculation, but the manual is explicit and doesn't mention light at all).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: confirmed wire 5 purple. before blind cuts, is there any condition based on display number, light color, strip colors, or keypad that changes which wire, or is it always wire 5 no matter what? thumbs up if always wire 5 regardless, thumbs down if conditional.

The manual only says "Cut the purple wire" - no conditions mentioned at all. It's unconditional.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
